text:
Situation: Epinephrine has been on FDA's shortage list since 2012-02-22 and remains current as of 2026-10-21. Current inventory across Corvale sites ranges from 3.3 to 25 days of supply. The 0.3 mg/0.3 mL syringe at Corvale East has the lowest coverage at 3.3 days.

Why (FDA record): FDA first posted the shortage on 2012-02-22. Import alert 66-66 was published on 2009-09-30, 875 days before the shortage posting. Inspection 762138 ended 2012-01-04 with a VAI classification, 49 days before the shortage posting. Inspection 808119 ended 2012-11-12 with an OAI classification, 264 days after the shortage posting. A Warning Letter was issued on 2013-05-06, 439 days after the shortage posting.

Our position: Supply is critically low for multiple presentations, particularly syringes at Corvale East. Viatris Specialty LLC is the rule-based best option and is not on FDA's shortage list today.

Recommended actions:
1. Buyer initiates purchase from Viatris Specialty LLC; requires Pharmacy Director approval.
2. Buyer qualifies kaleo, Inc. as secondary source; requires Pharmacy Director approval.
3. Buyer evaluates American Regent, Inc., Amneal Pharmaceuticals LLC, and Amneal Pharmaceuticals Private Limited for contract addition; requires P&T Committee approval for formulary changes.

Not recommended: Delaying procurement pending further FDA updates given the 14-year shortage duration and current low days-on-hand.
